original_question: For generic holomorphic foliations on the complex projective plane P2, are generic leaves dense?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Introduction: the unnumbered basic question "Are leaves dense for generic foliations?"; for the P^2-specialized stand-alone version, Section 4, Problem 4.1 supplies the paper's explicit convention that "generic leaves" means all leaves except countably many. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right ambient surface (the complex projective plane P^2), the right objects (holomorphic foliations), and the right dynamical property (density of leaves for generic foliations). That is very close to the paper's introductory density question, specialized to the surface case treated explicitly later in Sections 4 and 5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
missing_details: The paper's density question is not stated as a numbered conjecture or theorem; it appears only as an unnumbered basic question in the introduction. A stand-alone reformulation therefore has to specify the parameter space in which "generic" is being taken. Section 1 sets this up by discussing the space of holomorphic foliations of a fixed geometric degree. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Your draft does not fix the degree. In the paper, foliations are organized degree by degree, and the relevant notion is a generic foliation in the degree-d parameter space. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The paper's setup constructs degree-d foliations on projective space from a nonzero homogeneous holomorphic vector field on C^3 whose coefficients are homogeneous polynomials of one fixed degree and have no non-trivial common divisor; that background is implicit in your draft but needed for a paper-faithful stand-alone version. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Your draft does not specify what "generic leaves" means. The paper gives an explicit convention in Problem 4.1: generic leaves means all leaves except countably many of them. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Your draft does not say whether density is meant in P^2 itself or only in the nonsingular locus P^2 \ Sing(F). Because the paper separately asks in Problem 5.1 whether every leaf closure meets the singular set, a faithful density question should be read as density in the ambient projective plane P^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The foliation is singular in general, with leaves lying in the complement of the finite singular set; that singular setting is part of the paper's framework and should remain implicit or explicit in the refined version. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The draft does not identify the sense of "generic" (relative to the parameter space of degree-d foliations). The paper does not fully formalize that adjective here, so the safest paper-faithful rewrite is to keep the word generic but tie it explicitly to the degree-d parameter space introduced in Section 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
refined_question: Fix a geometric degree d and consider the parameter space of singular holomorphic foliations by Riemann surfaces on the complex projective plane P^2(C) of degree d, obtained from nonzero homogeneous holomorphic vector fields on C^3 whose coefficients are homogeneous polynomials of one fixed degree and have no non-trivial common divisor. For a generic foliation in this degree-d space, are all generic leaves—meaning all leaves except countably many—dense in P^2(C)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
justification: The draft is closest to the exact introductory sentence "Are leaves dense for generic foliations?" rather than to any broader neighboring problem. Because the paper does not restate that sentence as a numbered problem, the sharpest stand-alone version is to place it in the fixed-degree parameter space described in Section 1 and import the paper's explicit definition of "generic leaves" from Problem 4.1. I did not replace it with Problem 5.1, because Problem 5.1 asks only whether every leaf closure meets the singular set, which is related but not the same question as density of generic leaves. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
